abstract_literal_selector_local_existenc.selector: f_minus on F<0; f_plus on F>=0
hypotheses: F is C1 near the interface state (or sufficiently differentiable for the stated Lie derivatives).
Each branch field is continuous in time/state and locally Lipschitz in state on a one-sided neighborhood.
Branch expressions are finite/defined on the chosen neighborhood.
abstract_literal_selector_local_existenc.sufficient_condition: L_minus F < 0 OR L_plus F > 0 at F=0
abstract_literal_selector_local_existenc.reason: If L_plus F>0, the classical plus-branch IVP enters F>0 and satisfies the literal selector. Otherwise the disjunction supplies L_minus F<0; the minus-branch IVP enters F<0. The equality-assigned plus value at the single initial instant is measure-zero and does not violate the Caratheodory a.e. equation.
abstract_literal_selector_local_existenc.uniqueness: NOT_CLAIMED; if both self-side inequalities hold, two local continuations may exist.

pion_mapping.literal_selector: HMLA on F<0; SWIFT on F>=0 where the SWIFT fit is active
pion_mapping.certificate_used: N_HMLA,z>0 OR N_SWIFT,z<0, equivalently L_HMLA F<0 OR L_SWIFT F>0 in u=ln(a)
pion_mapping.conclusion: The formal local existence implication required at the qualified Pion interface is satisfied.

swift_fit_lower_boundary.source_rule: Inside SWIFT mode, when Pion>=PION_MAX, TR below the first fit node routes to HMLA; at/above the first node routes to SWIFT.
swift_fit_lower_boundary.nature: fixed background/time threshold, not a state-dependent interface
swift_fit_lower_boundary.conclusion: It does not create a trapping/sliding state interface; ordinary piecewise-in-time Caratheodory continuation applies if each adjacent branch is locally defined.

refined_unresolved_gate.first_normal: v_u = A(1-v)-v with A=rate_gamma_b/H; at v=1/10, tangency occurs at A=1/9.
refined_unresolved_gate.why_old_first_order_clearance_is_insuffi: The PEEBLES and non-PEEBLES arms share the same first thermal normal at a common state, but that normal may be exactly zero. Equality of a zero first normal does not in general imply literal-selector existence; tangential branch differences can determine the first nonzero higher-order departure.
refined_unresolved_gate.required_viability_test: On the exact tangent set, certify PEEBLES has the first nonzero normal derivative toward v<1/10 or the non-PEEBLES arm has it toward v>1/10; if the second derivative can vanish, continue to the first nonzero order rather than assume clearance.

domain_reduction.non_peebles_arm_in_this_strip: HMLA, because the entire strip is far below the 1775 K SWIFT-fit lower boundary; therefore the Pion HMLA/SWIFT interface is not the active complication here.

counterexample_check.purpose: Demonstrate why equal zero first normals are not a general existence theorem.

plus IVP gives x=-t^2/2<0, contradicting plus-side validity
